items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: There was a good friend of mine, his name was Edward Bordeaux.

ctx.x: Now, the people in those previous generations, did they play what you'd call jams?

Well, when I first started playing Dick, I can remember back that I knew a few piano players that played piano. And it seemed as though to me they played the real old ragtime piano. There was a good friend of mine, his name was Edward Bordeaux. I happen to think of him today, since I was coming up to this interview. The last I heard of him, he went to Memphis, and he was living there. But he never did play anywhere professionally. But he used to play a real good ragtime piano. And I used to just look for him to…
How were you when you went to see Mrs. Asset?

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1965-09-13
items.q: And I'd just go crazy to just listen to him play these rags. And he played them very, very mechanical and with not too much relaxation. But it was really one of the probably the oiliest influences that I had.

ctx.x: Were there any particular bands or specific musicians who were especially encouraging when you were just trying to get into the jazz or if you will ragtime playing?

Right. There were no specific musicians, Charlie, in the early period because if you will figure this, that I started taking lessons when I was about eight or nine years old. And, of course, that's pretty young, you know, especially when you go back into those old days and people, the way they were, you know, kind of strict, you didn't get much chance to get out too much. Right. I didn't meet too many musicians. I wasn't around too many musicians. But there was one man, his name was Edward Bordeaux. I have never…
Would you remember how you spelled his name, Bordeaux, you said?
